title: Fan Cowl Latch Change with Positive Visual Indication of an Unlatched Condition

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Fan cowl latch replacement giving an unlatched cowl a visible red indication from ground level, after three departures with the fan cowl unlatched and one cowl loss during the take-off roll.

sections.reason: Three departures with a fan cowl unlatched were reported across the fleet in two years, one of which ended with the cowl departing the aircraft during the take-off roll and damaging the flap. In every case the walk-around had been done and the latch had been left hanging in a position that is hard to see from ground level with the engine in its installed attitude. The investigation found no fault with the latch mechanism itself; the finding was that a correctly latched cowl and an unlatched one look almost identical from the only place a crew member ever stands.
sections.description: The latch assembly is replaced by a unit whose keeper carries a red painted flag that is mechanically driven out of the cowl line when the latch is not fully engaged, and which cannot be stowed unless the hook is over centre. The seal D7110121607820 at the latch aperture is replaced to clear the flag travel, the clamp D7110124986440 is changed for a shorter item and the nozzle sub-assembly D7110129326915 is re-positioned. The shroud kit AR674643-02 and the nozzle assembly CAD746437-78 are re-issued with the flag cut-out. Washers EN17059-86 are renewed at each latch. Functional item 89EN6, the latch position bracket, is affected. Work is at the fan cowl in zones 452 and 453 and at the pylon bracket in zone 432. Installation detail is on drawing D71101265891.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 1.6 kg per engine, symmetric, with no centre of gravity effect worth declaring. No electrical load change. The latch is not interchangeable with the delivered latch because the keeper aperture in the cowl changes, and a mixed installation on one cowl is prohibited and stated on the placard. The walk-around item in the flight crew procedures is reworded because the crew now looks for the absence of a red flag rather than for the position of a handle. Maintenance manual and illustrated parts content both change.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00342 in September 2020. Retrofit is by Service Bulletin CRN-71-2002 and was made a fleet campaign at the request of two authorities, with a compliance time of thirty months. Six hours per engine at a line stop, cowl removal not required.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation on both nacelles, no declared effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00342, cowl aperture change absorbed at the nacelle supplier
